findings.description: The three hung-server tests each sleep 2s inside the handler, and `defer hung.Close()` blocks until the outstanding handler returns, so each test costs ~2s regardless of the 150ms client timeout. This takes the actuator package - which holds the CI 'completeness teeth' (completeness_test.go:4-9) and is therefore run constantly - from ~0.1s to ~6.2s, a 62x increase.
findings.evidence: Measured with `go test -count=1 ./internal/actuator/` on both exported trees: origin/main `ok github.com/phorvex/phorvex/internal/actuator 0.099s`; fix/postjson-timeout-classification `ok github.com/phorvex/phorvex/internal/actuator 6.184s`. Source: gpu_stack_unreachable_test.go:22-24, :56-58, :71-73 each contain `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` with `defer hung.Close()`.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sleep with a release channel: `block := make(chan struct{}); defer close(block)` declared before `defer hung.Close()` (so it runs first), and `<-block` in the handler. Same coverage, ~0s. Alternatively share one hung server across the three tests.

findings.description: The substring arm ('refused', 'no such host', 'Client.Timeout', 'context deadline exceeded') is dead for anything produced by http.Client.Do: every such error is a *url.Error, which implements net.Error, so errors.As(err, &ne) already returns true first. TestIsUnreachableRefusedAndDNS therefore 'keeps the pre-existing cases covered' only by feeding hand-written errors.New(...) strings - it exercises the one arm production never reaches, which is exactly the shortcut the new file's own header criticises ('so the error string is Go's own, not a hand-written approximation'). That arm is also the only part that can misfire, since it will classify any wrapped domain error whose message contains 'refused' as unreachable.

findings.description: Cross-module regression in the forensic/scoring path. adapter-rotate's errStackUnreachable branch only sets a note and then falls through to write `phorvex.ai/adapter-epoch` and return Emitted:true. The console attack watcher treats ANY bump of that annotation as proof the poison was evicted. Before this PR a client timeout on UnloadAdapter was a hard error, so no epoch was written and the attack was honestly scored LANDED; after this PR the same timeout takes the unreachable branch, the epoch is bumped, and the console reports Outcome=DEFENDED / Actuated=true while the poisoned LoRA is still loaded. This fires exactly under the load the commit message targets ("a saturated stack TIMES OUT where an absent one REFUSES"). The project already fixed this exact anti-pattern for kv-reset (handlers_ai.go:287-299 returns Emitted:false and writes no epoch, commented "a flush epoch for a flush that never ran is a false forensic record") but adapter-rotate was not brought in line, and this PR widens when its unreachable branch is reached.

Consumer phorvex/internal/console/attack_results.go:262 `if ep := s.podAnno(r.Namespace, r.Pod, "phorvex.ai/adapter-epoch"); ep != "" && ep != epoch0 { r.Outcome, r.Action, r.Actuated = "DEFENDED", "adapter-rotate", true }`. Contrast phorvex/internal/actuator/handlers_ai.go:295 `return HandlerResult{Emitted: false, MutationKind: "none", ...}` for the same unreachable case in kv-reset.
findings.suggested_fix: In adapterRotateHandler.Enact, treat the errStackUnreachable case the way kv-reset does: skip the `phorvex.ai/adapter-epoch` annotation/label write (or write a distinct `phorvex.ai/adapter-rotate-pending` marker the watcher ignores) and return Emitted:false, so a rotation whose unload never reached the stack is not scored as a defence. Same reasoning applies to the annoKVEpoch write at handlers_ai_p4set.go:391 in the kv-migrate-invalidate unreachable branch.

findings.description: errors.As(err, &ne) on net.Error collapses the documented tri-state: *url.Error implements net.Error, and http.Client.Do wraps essentially every failure in *url.Error, so postJSON now returns errStackUnreachable even when the serving stack demonstrably ANSWERED, or when the request never left the process. I confirmed three concrete cases where the pre-PR postJSON classifier returned a hard error (correct case (c) fail-closed) and the new one returns "unreachable" (case (b) PENDING): a redirect loop (the stack answered 302 ten times, e.g. an auth proxy bouncing to a login page), context canceled (operator shutdown / parent reconcile cancel - nothing to do with the stack), and unsupported protocol scheme (a config error). The file header at gpu_stack.go:15-19 is explicit that case (c) must FAIL-CLOSED. This affects all five P4-set methods (UnloadAdapter/LoadAdapter/DrainRequests/ApplyVariant/InvalidateLocal), which now silently report [PENDING-GPU-VALIDATION] for misconfiguration. do() already had this branch, so the widening is new only for postJSON.
findings.evidence: gpu_stack.go:130-133 `var ne net.Error; if errors.As(err, &ne) { return true }`. Measured with the helper body copied verbatim out of the PR: `redirect-loop: err=Post "http://127.0.0.1:36315/again": stopped after 10 redirects  isUnreachable=true  oldPostJSON=false`; `ctx-cancel: err=Post "http://127.0.0.1:34937": context canceled  isUnreachable=true  oldPostJSON=false`; `bad-scheme: err=Post "httpx://1.2.3.4:8000/v1/drain": unsupported protocol scheme "httpx"  isUnreachable=true  oldPostJSON=false`. Contrast gpu_stack.go:15-19 `(c) endpoint REACHABLE but the call FAILS   -> FAIL-CLOSED (return the error; never claim success).`
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow the net.Error branch to transport failures that really mean "nobody answered": `if errors.As(err, &ne) && ne.Timeout() { return true }` plus explicit *net.OpError / *net.DNSError / ECONNREFUSED checks, and drop errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) (a canceled parent context is an aborted operation, not an unreachable stack - and the request may well have been executed server-side). Everything else should keep falling through to the hard-error path.

findings.description: The substring checks the PR adds as its headline fix are unreachable from both call sites. Because http.Client.Do always wraps transport failures in *url.Error, which satisfies net.Error, the errors.As branch returns first for every error do()/postJSON can see; "Client.Timeout", "context deadline exceeded", "refused" and "no such host" are never evaluated in production. The behaviour change actually comes from the net.Error branch, not from the string matching the comment describes. Correspondingly TestIsUnreachableRefusedAndDNS feeds hand-built errors.New(...) values that no production path can produce, so it does not guard the real classifier; only the three hung-server tests exercise real behaviour.

findings.component: isUnreachable classifier — case (b) vs case (c) split
findings.description: gpu_stack.go documents two distinct classes: (b) 'no serving stack answered' → PENDING/emit-with-caveat, and (c) 'reachable-but-failing endpoint' → fail-closed. isUnreachable returns true for ANY error satisfying net.Error, and *url.Error satisfies net.Error unconditionally, so errors that prove the stack IS reachable — notably a redirect loop, which requires the endpoint to have answered 10+ times — are now classified as case (b) by postJSON. A compromised/poisoned serving stack could therefore force every postJSON-backed move (adapter unload, drain, guardrail apply, KV invalidate) into the permissive PENDING branch (epoch written, Emitted:true) instead of the fail-closed branch. do() had this hole already; the PR extends it to postJSON.

refuted.why_dropped:
The mechanical trace is accurate (timeout -> errStackUnreachable -> drainPending=true, err=nil -> falls through to Delete), but the finding's premise — that pre-PR the old leader survived a timed-out drain, and that the PR newly exposes in-flight requests — is refuted by three things in the same tree:

1) The pre-PR "wedge" already deleted the old leader anyway, WITHOUT any drain. warmCutover relabels the leader role=retiring at handlers_ai.go:136 BEFORE the drain, so a hard error at handlers_ai.go:147-148 returns with the pod already labeled `retiring`. The runner calls reconcileWedged -> actuator.ResumeWarmSwaps every tick, independent of tenant cadence (phorvex/internal/runner/manager.go:187-196), and warmswap_resume.go:33-41 unconditionally `c.Delete`s every pod with `labels[phorvex.ai/role]==retiring` in any swap-group namespace — no drain, no receipt. So on origin/main the exact overload scenario ended in "old leader deleted with requests in flight" one tick later, with strictly LESS drain effort and a receipt saying Emitted:false. The PR does not create that outcome; it moves it into the same reconcile and records it.

2) "Drain result gates the delete" is not an invariant of this codebase; warmCutover was the outlier. handlers_ai_p4set.go:110-111 (groupCoherentCutover) does `_, _, _ = drainInflight(ctx, ec, old)` then `_ = ec.Client.Delete(ctx, old)` — discarding even hard errors. handlers_ai.go:240-241 (mig-rebind) does `_, drainPending, _ := drainInflight(...)` then deletes. The PR aligns warmCutover with both.

3) "requests still in flight" overstates the impact. `ec.Client.Delete(ctx, leader)` (handlers_ai.go:150) carries no DeleteOptions — the only options-bearing delete in the package is handlers_k8s.go:57 and that is a UID precondition, not GracePeriodSeconds(0). So this is a graceful delete: kubelet SIGTERMs and honors the pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds, and step (2) already routed new admits away via role=retiring. The K8s route-drain + grace window is exactly what the comment at handlers_ai.go:144-145 says applies when the stack-side abort is pending.

On the sub-claim that the receipt "asserts a false fact": errStackUnreachable is DEFINED in this codebase, pre-dating the PR, as "no serving stack answered (connection refused/timeout/no IP)" (gpu_stack.go:100-101). Timeout is explicitly inside the documented meaning of "unreachable", and the note is already tagged [PENDING-GPU-VALIDATION]. At most the wording at handlers_ai.go:158 is imprecise for the busy-stack case — a cosmetic nit in a file this PR does not touch, hence info, not warn.

Side note on realism: the drain route is `/v1/drain`, documented at gpu_stack_p4set.go:35 as "[PENDING-GPU-VALIDATION] no standard vLLM drain-all; deployment-specific", so against stock vLLM the saturated-stack case answers 404 and takes the reachable-but-failing fail-closed branch (DrainRequests, gpu_stack_p4set.go:121-123), not the timeout branch.

If the reviewer wants the 3s client timeout (gpu_stack.go:159 on the branch, :130 on main) raised for drains, that is a separate pre-existing concern this PR neither introduces nor worsens.

The transport mechanism the reviewer describes is real (*url.Error does implement net.Error, so EOF and redirect-loop now hit the sentinel in postJSON), but the claim AS STATED is wrong on the three points that make it a warn.

(1) "POST-CONNECT failures where the serving stack demonstrably ANSWERED" is false for the dominant case. I reproduced all four cases with a standalone Go probe (/tmp/urlerrprobe/main.go): a hijack+close yields `Post "http://127.0.0.1:45895": EOF` — *url.Error carrying io.EOF with ZERO response bytes. Nothing answered; the socket was accepted and then died, which on a kube Pod IP is the classic "endpoint is gone / kube-proxy accepted for a dead backend" signal, i.e. case (b), not (c). The repo itself defines "ANSWERED" as "returned an HTTP status" — gpu_stack_p4set.go:86-89 `// 404 ... the stack ANSWERED`. Only the redirect-loop example genuinely answered, and that is pathological for a vLLM admin POST.

(2) Case (c) is untouched by this PR. FAIL-CLOSED for reachable-but-failing is implemented by the okCode status checks at gpu_stack_p4set.go:95, :111, :124, :160, :186 — every one still returns a hard error. The PR changes only the `resp, err := c.hc.Do(req)` transport branch.

(3) The boundary the reviewer objects to is pre-existing, shipped behaviour, not something the PR invents. do() on merge-base already had the identical `var ne net.Error; if errors.As(err, &ne)` branch (gpu_stack.go:143-144 pre-PR). My probe confirms that classifier returns true for EOF, redirect loop AND client timeout. ResetPrefixCache — the kv-reset path the reviewer cites as the precedent — goes through do() (gpu_stack.go:177), so kv-reset has ALWAYS treated an EOF as unreachable. The PR only stops postJSON drifting from that, which is its stated purpose.

(4) The "same class of false-defence accounting as the kv-reset FAIL-CLOSED FIX" analogy is inverted. kv-reset's fix (handlers_ai.go:283-294) addressed a case where NOTHING happened yet Emitted:true. In guardrailRotateHandler a real, reversible K8s mutation has already committed at handlers_ai_p4set.go:317 before the stack call at :322, and the PENDING note at :327 explicitly says "variant re-keyed in K8s, not applied to the live filter" — honest, not a claimed defence. And main's behaviour for an EOF is strictly WORSE: the default branch at :330 returns `HandlerResult{}` + error after the Pod was already re-keyed, so MutationKind is "" and RollbackRef is empty — an orphaned, unrollbackable mutation. That is exactly the half-completed-cutover failure this PR exists to fix.

Residual worth an info note only: for kvMigrateInvalidateHandler an unreachable classification still writes annoKVEpoch (:390-392) and Emitted:true (:396) for a KV invalidate that did not run, which is arguably the false-forensic-record pattern kv-reset removed — but that is pre-existing for genuine unreachability and is not introduced or widened in kind by this PR.

Those are different facts: cancellation means the operator gave up (manager shutdown, or the per-tick deadline at runner/manager.go:180 with the default 4x BaseInterval capped at 2 min). An action aborted by our own shutdown is now reported as '[PENDING-GPU-VALIDATION] serving stack unreachable'. Blast radius is limited because the follow-on ec.Client.Update/Delete calls share the dead ctx and fail anyway - except guardrail-rotate, which does its K8s Update at handlers_ai_p4set.go:317 BEFORE ApplyVariant at :322, so a cancel in that window yields Emitted:true.
refuted.why_dropped:
The finding's mechanism, its trigger, and its consequence all fail verification.

1) The cited line is INERT — it is not what folds cancellation into "unreachable". `http.Client.Do` always wraps transport errors in `*url.Error`, which satisfies `net.Error` (it has Timeout()/Temporary()), so `errors.As(err, &ne)` on PR gpu_stack.go:126-128 already returns true for a cancelled ctx and returns before line 129 is ever evaluated. I verified this empirically with a pre-cancelled ctx against a hung httptest server: `err="Post \"http://127.0.0.1:36263\": context canceled" type=*url.Error`, `errors.As(net.Error)=true`. Deleting the `context.Canceled` clause the reviewer objects to would change zero observable behaviour. And that `errors.As(err, &ne)` branch is copied VERBATIM from origin/main gpu_stack.go:144 — so "context.Canceled classifies as errStackUnreachable" is the pre-existing do() contract on main, not a new design decision by this PR. The PR merely stops postJSON (main gpu_stack_p4set.go:63, substring-only) from disagreeing with do() — which is the PR's entire stated purpose.

2) The cited trigger is wrong. runner/manager.go:180 is `context.WithTimeout(ctx, m.PerTickTimeout)`; an expiring WithTimeout yields context.DeadlineExceeded, NOT context.Canceled, and `cancel()` at :182 runs only after `m.tick(tctx)` has returned. So the per-tick deadline never delivers Canceled to a handler. Only a full manager shutdown (parent ctx cancel) can, and it would have to land in the microsecond window between two adjacent statements.

3) The named blast radius is the intended, safer behaviour, not a defect. At handlers_ai_p4set.go:317 the `ec.Client.Update` has already SUCCEEDED before ApplyVariant at :322, so a real reversible pod-annotation mutation exists. handler.go:58-60 documents the contract: "Emitted is false only for the declared-not-implemented handler (disable); every real handler that mutates sets it true." runner/manager.go:645-651 copies RollbackRef/ObjectsTouched/MutationKind into the audit ONLY when Emitted is true; on the hard-error path dispatch returns an empty Result and manager.go:641-644 just logs "actuate failed" and continues. So origin/main's behaviour here loses the rollback reference for a mutation that really happened — precisely the half-completed/Emitted:false wedge class this PR exists to fix. The PR's Emitted:true with note "variant re-keyed in K8s, not applied to the live filter" is the more accurate report.

The only literally-true part of the finding is that postJSON's classification of a cancelled ctx changes (main: hard error; PR: errStackUnreachable) — but the attributed cause is the wrong line, the attributed trigger cannot produce Canceled, and the flagged outcome is an improvement, so the finding does not stand as stated.

result.summary:
## Verdict: request changes — the fix is right, the classifier is too wide, and it widens a path that writes a false "DEFENDED" record

The root cause is real and the fix earns its place. `postJSON` matched lowercase `"timeout"`, which never appears in Go's client-timeout error (`context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`), so every postJSON-backed action (adapter unload, drain, guardrail apply, KV invalidate) hard-errored instead of taking its `errStackUnreachable` branch. I confirmed this by exporting the branch, reverting both classifiers, and re-running: `TestPostJSONTimeoutSurfacesUnreachable` fails with exactly that string and passes on the PR tree. `go vet` and the package tests pass.

Three things should be resolved before merge.

### 1. `isUnreachable` collapses the documented case (b) / case (c) split — `gpu_stack.go:130-133`

`errors.As(err, &net.Error)` is true for essentially every error `http.Client.Do` returns, because `*url.Error` implements `net.Error`. The file header (`gpu_stack.go:15-19`) says case (c) — endpoint reachable but call fails — must FAIL-CLOSED. Measured against the PR's helper body, three cases flip from hard error (old postJSON) to "unreachable":

```
redirect-loop: stopped after 10 redirects            isUnreachable=true  oldPostJSON=false
ctx-cancel:    context canceled                       isUnreachable=true  oldPostJSON=false
bad-scheme:    unsupported protocol scheme "httpx"     isUnreachable=true  oldPostJSON=false
```

A redirect loop means the stack answered ten times; `context canceled` means the operator shut down. Neither is "no stack answered". Suggest narrowing to `errors.As(err, &ne) && ne.Timeout()` plus explicit `*net.OpError` / `*net.DNSError` / `ECONNREFUSED` / `context.DeadlineExceeded`, and dropping `context.Canceled`. `do()` already had this hole; the PR extends it to the five P4-set methods.

Corollary: the substring tail (`"refused"`, `"no such host"`, `"Client.Timeout"`, …) is **dead code** for anything `Do` returns — the `net.Error` branch always returns first. The headline described in the commit message is not what changes behaviour; the `net.Error` branch is.

### 2. Widening reaches adapter-rotate's unreachable branch, which still stamps the forensic epoch

`handlers_ai_p4set.go:180-182` sets a note on `errStackUnreachable`, falls through, writes `phorvex.ai/adapter-epoch` (`:205`) and returns `Emitted:true`. `internal/console/attack_results.go:262` treats any bump of that annotation as proof the poison was evicted → `Outcome=DEFENDED, Actuated=true`. Pre-PR a header timeout hit the `default:` hard error and nothing was written; post-PR it writes a DEFENDED record while the poisoned LoRA is still loaded. The newly-reachable case is the dangerous one: a dial failure already produced lowercase `i/o timeout`, whereas a stack that *accepts the connection and never answers* is a live, saturated stack.

The branch itself is pre-existing; what the PR changes is how often it is reached — and the commit message explicitly targets saturation. The project already fixed exactly this for kv-reset (`handlers_ai.go:288-297`: `Emitted:false`, no epoch, commented "a flush epoch for a flush that never ran is a false forensic record"). Adapter-rotate should be brought in line, or the widening should be held until it is.

Related: the "honest PENDING" signal lives only in `HandlerResult.Note` (`handler.go:61`), which nothing reads — `dispatch` doesn't copy it into `Result`, `Result` has no such field, and `audit.Record` has no equivalent. So a timeout-driven partial actuation serializes byte-identically to a successful one and increments `phorvex_actuations_total` the same way. A `Pending bool` threaded through to the audit record would make the new class filterable.

### 3. Test wall time: actuator package goes 0.099s → 6.184s (62x)

`go test -count=1 ./internal/actuator/` — main `0.099s`, PR branch `6.184s`. Each of the three hung-server tests does `time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)` in the handler (`gpu_stack_unreachable_test.go:22-24, :56-58, :71-73`) while `defer hung.Close()` blocks until the handler returns, so each pays ~2s even though the client gives up at 150ms. This package holds the CI completeness teeth (`completeness_test.go:4-9`) and runs constantly. Fix: a release channel closed before `Close()`, or one shared hung server.

### Smaller test notes

- `gpu_stack_unreachable_test.go:42-43` — the block commented "Guard the specific regression" only calls `t.Logf`, so it can never fail. Make it `t.Errorf` or delete it.
- `TestIsUnreachableRefusedAndDNS` feeds hand-written `errors.New` strings that no production path produces (real refused/DNS errors are `*url.Error` and short-circuit on `net.Error`), so it covers only the dead substring arm — the exact shortcut the file's own header criticises.
- `TestDoTimeoutSurfacesUnreachable` and `TestIsUnreachableOnRealClientTimeout` both still pass with `do()` reverted to its pre-PR form (it already had `errors.As(err, &ne)`), so they pin a contract rather than catch this bug. Worth saying so in their comments.
- No negative test on the real path: nothing pins that a TLS/scheme/redirect failure still hard-errors, which is what makes finding #1 easy to regress.

### Checked and found clean

`warmCutover`'s drain-then-delete path (the timeout does not cause the old leader to be deleted on a pending drain), the request-drain `phorvex.ai/serving` label sequencing (pre-existing, unchanged by this PR), and the `LoadAdapter` call sites (`handlers_ai_p4set.go:189, :236` are the only postJSON-backed sites with no `errStackUnreachable` branch, but behaviour there is unchanged by this PR — worth a follow-up, not a blocker).
